theorem: If a positive contraction C has exact kernel projector P, maximum row support s and all-state gap gamma, and some projector row has mass m on columns with squared entries <=a, then for D=ln(m/(2a))/ln(s+1)>1, gamma <=[ln(8/m)/(4(D-1))]². The endpoint gamma=1 implies m<=a(s+1).
proof: RESULT B: exact Chebyshev approximate projector with error <=2exp(-2t sqrt gamma), row support <=(s+1)^t, and best sparse-row approximation mass lower bound.
inputs: Exact kernel/projector-row parameters and positive-contraction normalization. No graph law, covariance, stoquasticity or local-constraint decomposition.
cost: Mathematical bound only; Chebyshev filtering is not a free dense row oracle. Its coefficient and exponentially growing row costs remain charged.
strongest_control: Standard Chebyshev AGSP prior art; new scoped combination with exact row degree and projector distribution.
falsifier: Exact positive C and projector row satisfying the stated parameters with gamma exceeding the explicit bound.
validation: Full derivation and exact rational scalar polynomial fixtures; not formal/external validation.

proof: RESULT A,C: a phi-tail projector row has q8^T flat psi-tail entries of squared magnitude 1/(K²8^T), hence mass q/K². Apply B.
